podcast.body: Co-written by Bill Freeze and Chip Davis, this trucker and CB radio anthem perfectly captured the mid-70s Citizens Band radio fad. It became a phenomenon, topping Billboard's Hot Country Singles chart for a six-week run just before Christmas 1975, and then reaching number one on the Hot 100 in early January 1976. "convoy reached number one on billboards hot country singles chart and settled in for a six-week run on top."

podcast.body: Co-written with Chip Davis, this single was released in November 1975. It became a time capsule of trucker life in the mid-70s, featuring CB slang and telling a story of protest against the 55 mph speed limit, toll roads, and the difficulties faced by the trucking industry. The narrator, Rubberduck, leads a growing group of vehicles. The song hit number one on the Billboard Hot 100 in January 1976 and held the number one spot on the country chart for six weeks. Rolling Stone ranked it number 98 on its list of the top 100 country songs of all time, and it inspired a 1978 movie. "Convoy is a time capsule of trucker life in the mid-70s."
